blindSummary: No criminalisation of trans presence and no legislative reform at the state/province level on legal gender recognition as of March 2025, but the civil registry runs an administrative procedure built on a 2019 top-court ruling that struck down the civil code's judicial-process requirement. This state/province also appears repeatedly as one of the units where lethal violence against LGBTQ+ people concentrates: it is repeatedly named among those units and recorded 6 victims in the 2021 national annual count (19 of 32 units had victims that year). Functioning recognition machinery is offset by a documented lethal-violence footprint.
blindSourceSummaries: An international human-rights group's state-by-state tracker on legal gender recognition in the country (March 2025), covering which of the 32 units have legislated an administrative procedure and the top-court rulings that drove expansion. For this unit: no legislative reform as of March 2025, but an administrative procedure exists via a 2019 top-court ruling invalidating the civil code's judicial requirement.

An international human-rights group's report (6 March 2024) on a neighbouring unit: no legal gender recognition procedure there exposes trans people to institutional mistreatment - the August 2023 killing of an activist remained unsolved, hate-motivation provisions are absent from that unit's criminal code, and healthcare staff routinely out patients by calling legal names. Baseline for how a unit without any procedure behaves.

A national newspaper (24 July 2024): the capital city made transfemicide a crime with sentences up to 70 years (a law approved 18 July 2024), in a setting documented as among the deadliest for trans people in the region; over 95% of homicides nationally went unpunished in 2022.
blindOutOfScope: General cartel violence, kidnapping and theft drive foreign travel advisories for parts of the country and affect all travellers equally; they do not move trans-specific risk here.
blindLocalsOnly: Recognition here runs through a court-forced registry procedure rather than a statute - a resident documents question that does not touch visitors.
